source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN Examination, 7th ed.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Mang Pedro, 62, is in the coronary care unit recovering from an acute MI.
questions.stem: Mang Pedro is very anxious. Which intervention is the PRIORITY?
options: Have family present for all care
questions.rationale: Accurate information reduces fear and builds trust. Detailed explanations can raise anxiety, so information is given simply and clearly.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q911 (PDF p. 1154)
questions.quote: Accurate information reduces fear, strengthens the nurse–client relationship

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Mang Pedro, 62, is in the coronary care unit recovering from an acute MI.
questions.stem: On day 4, Mang Pedro refuses to dangle his legs: 'Only if my doctor says so.' What behavior is this?
questions.rationale: Dependency shows as refusing any activity unless the provider specifically approves it.
explanations: Correct: relies on the provider's approval.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q934 (PDF p. 1178)
questions.quote: Dependency is one response that may be manifested by the client’s refusal to perform any tasks or activities unless specifically approved

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Mang Pedro, 62, is in the coronary care unit recovering from an acute MI.
questions.stem: The evening before discharge, which action by Mang Pedro suggests DENIAL?
options: He asks for a sleeping pill
He eats only a quarter of supper
He walks up three flights of stairs alone
questions.rationale: Ignoring activity limits and avoiding lifestyle changes are signs of denial. Stair climbing should be supervised at this stage.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q912 (PDF p. 1155)
questions.quote: Ignoring activity limitations and avoiding lifestyle changes are signs of the denial stage.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.situation: Mang Pedro, 62, is in the coronary care unit recovering from an acute MI.
questions.stem: The nurse finds Mang Pedro quietly crying, with no physical cause. What is the BEST response?
options: 'Can you tell me what's upsetting you?'
questions.rationale: Clients after MI often feel anxious or afraid. An open question showing genuine interest lets him express his concerns.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q977 (PDF p. 1226)
questions.quote: The nurse allows the client to express concerns by showing genuine interest and concern

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client in acute pulmonary edema is severely anxious. Which action meets his needs holistically?
options: Stay with him as much as possible
questions.rationale: Pulmonary edema brings extreme fear and a sense of impending doom. The nurse stays with the client as much as possible. Family can support him but cannot meet his physiological needs.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q980 (PDF p. 1229)
questions.quote: Because the client typically experiences a sense of impending doom, the nurse should remain with the client as much as possible.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Why is reducing anxiety a key strategy in acute pulmonary edema?
questions.rationale: Falling cardiac output triggers the sympathetic fight-or-flight response, which adds to the heart's workload. Reducing anxiety helps raise cardiac output and lower fluid volume.
explanations: Correct: less sympathetic load on the heart.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1000 (PDF p. 1251)
questions.quote: Reducing anxiety will help the client during treatment to increase cardiac output and decrease fluid volume.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with PVCs says, 'I'm afraid something bad will happen.' Which action gives the MOST immediate help?
options: Have staff stay with the client
questions.rationale: A calm, safe environment, appropriate reassurance, touch, and someone staying with the client ease fear.
explanations: Does not address the fear now.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q982 (PDF p. 1231)
questions.quote: having someone remain with the client as much as possible.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with Raynaud's disease has a stressful job and copes poorly. Which change should the nurse suggest?
questions.rationale: Stress triggers Raynaud's vasospasm, so a stress-management program or biofeedback training can help. Quitting the job is unrealistic.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q983 (PDF p. 1232)
questions.quote: Stress can trigger the vasospasm that occurs with Raynaud’s disease

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: During discharge teaching, a client with heart failure says, 'What's the use? I'll die anyway.' What is the likely cause?
questions.rationale: Anxiety and fear often develop after heart failure and can further strain the failing heart.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q990 (PDF p. 1240)
questions.quote: Anxiety and fear often develop after heart failure, and they can further tax the failing heart.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which statement about thrombophlebitis care shows effective learning?
questions.rationale: Elevation uses gravity to improve venous return, lower venous pressure, and relieve edema and pain.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1045 (PDF p. 1319)
questions.quote: The nurse plans to elevate the affected extremity because this facilitates venous return

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which statement by a client with a new ICD shows a need for MORE teaching?
options: 'I'll avoid rough contact over the site.'
'Tight belts over the site are fine.'
'I'll show my ID card at metal detectors.'
questions.rationale: Clients avoid tight clothing or belts over the ICD, rough contact, strong electromagnetic fields, and metal detectors.
explanations: Correct answer: tight belts are avoided.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1248 (PDF p. 1544)
questions.quote: Postdischarge instructions typically include avoiding the following: tight clothing or belts over the ICD insertion site

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client's ECG shows a PR interval of 0.16 seconds. How should the nurse interpret this?
questions.rationale: The normal PR interval is 0.12 to 0.20 seconds, so 0.16 is normal.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1263 (PDF p. 1564)
questions.quote: The PR interval range is 0.12 to 0.2 seconds.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which finding is an UNRELIABLE sign of antibiotic response in infective endocarditis?
questions.rationale: Once a murmur develops it does not resolve on its own, so it is the least reliable sign. Negative cultures and a normal temperature show the infection is clearing.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1297 (PDF p. 1599)
questions.quote: A systolic heart murmur, once present in the client, will not resolve spontaneously and is therefore the least reliable indicator.

questions.subject: NP V
questions.stem: The ECG complexes on the monitor are very small and hard to read. Which setting should the nurse check?
questions.rationale: The amplitude or 'gain' setting controls complex size and can be adjusted up or down.
explanations: Turns the machine on or off.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1298 (PDF p. 1599)
questions.quote: The amplitude, commonly called “gain,” regulates the size of the complex

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which assessment BEST detects the onset of heart failure in a client with valvular disease?
questions.rationale: New or increased crackles indicate fluid in the lungs from heart failure. The other findings are less reliable.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1310 (PDF p. 1612)
questions.quote: Breath sounds are the best way to assess for the onset of heart failure.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After fem-pop bypass, which question BEST detects graft occlusion?
options: 'Is it like the pain before surgery?'
questions.rationale: The most frequent sign of graft occlusion is the return of pain like the preoperative pain.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1312 (PDF p. 1614)
questions.quote: The most frequent indication that a graft is occluding is the return of pain that is similar to that experienced preoperatively.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After lifestyle changes for hypertension, which BP reading shows the MOST success?
questions.rationale: Normal BP is below 120/80. Of the options, 128/84 is closest to normal and shows the most success.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1313 (PDF p. 1615)
questions.quote: Normal blood pressure readings are less than 120/80 mm Hg.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client has a history of intermittent claudication. Which symptom should the nurse ask about?
options: Leg pain with exercise, relieved by rest
questions.rationale: Intermittent claudication is leg pain that comes on with exercise and is relieved by rest. It is the classic sign of peripheral arterial insufficiency.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1315 (PDF p. 1617)
questions.quote: Intermittent claudication is a symptom characterized by a sudden onset of leg pain that occurs with exercise and is relieved by rest.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which item should a client with a new permanent pacemaker avoid?
questions.rationale: Pacemakers are shielded from most electrical devices. Clients are warned about strong currents or magnetic fields such as store antitheft devices and airport metal detectors.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1336 (PDF p. 1639)
questions.quote: A pacemaker is shielded from interference from most electrical devices.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with frequent PVCs feels lightheaded after sitting up. What will the nurse likely hear on apical auscultation?
questions.rationale: PVCs make the rhythm irregular. The apical pulse is the most accurate way to assess rhythm; a radial pulse may miss beats.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1405 (PDF p. 1711)
questions.quote: When a client has PVCs, the rate is irregular

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which intervention reduces the risk of DVT after a vaginal hysterectomy?
questions.rationale: Ambulation, pneumatic compression boots, range-of-motion exercises, and antiembolism stockings prevent DVT after major surgery.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1421 (PDF p. 1727)
questions.quote: The client is at risk for deep vein thrombosis or thrombophlebitis after this surgery, as for any other major surgery.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which finding does the nurse expect in a client with polycythemia vera?
questions.rationale: Polycythemia vera raises blood viscosity and volume, causing a ruddy complexion, dusky red mucosa, hypertension, dizziness, headache, and fullness in the head.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1442 (PDF p. 1751)
questions.quote: Manifestations of polycythemia vera include a ruddy complexion, dusky red mucosa, hypertension, dizziness, headache

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which complication should the nurse monitor for in toxic shock syndrome?
questions.rationale: TSS, often linked to tampon use, can cause DIC. Signs are reported promptly.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1444 (PDF p. 1753)
questions.quote: DIC is a complication of TSS.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client has pernicious anemia. Disease of which organ affects vitamin B12 absorption?
questions.rationale: Vitamin B12 is absorbed in the ileum, so small bowel disease is a risk factor for pernicious anemia.
explanations: Correct: the site of B12 absorption.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1454 (PDF p. 1763)
questions.quote: Pernicious anemia can occur in a client who has a disease involving the ileum, where vitamin B12 is absorbed.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which finding is typical of pernicious anemia?
questions.rationale: Classic signs include weakness, mild diarrhea, and a smooth, sore, red tongue, plus neurologic signs such as paresthesias and balance problems.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1522 (PDF p. 1832)
questions.quote: Classic clinical indicators of pernicious anemia include weakness; mild diarrhea; and a smooth, sore, red tongue.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which laboratory value is elevated in sickle cell anemia?
questions.rationale: Sickle cell anemia is characterized by sickled hemoglobin (Hgb S). Two abnormal genes are needed for the disease; one gives sickle cell trait.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1458 (PDF p. 1767)
questions.quote: The client must have two abnormal genes yielding hemoglobin-S to have sickle cell anemia.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which sign should the nurse monitor MOST in a client in sickle cell crisis?
questions.rationale: Sickle cell crisis causes severe bone and joint pain from microvascular occlusion. Treatment includes opioids, oxygen, and IV fluids.
questions.source: Saunders Q&A Review for the NCLEX-RN, 7th ed., Q1461 (PDF p. 1770)
questions.quote: Sickle cell crisis usually causes severe pain in the bones and joints along with joint swelling.
